facts.claim: Processing can also induce leaching out of minerals and a reduced mineral bioaccessibility and bioavailability.
facts.quote: Although processing can have a positive effect, it also can induce leaching out of minerals and a reduced mineral bioaccessibility and bioavailability.

facts.claim: Adequate consumption of plant foods cannot fulfill the human body’s total nutrient requirement.
facts.quote: Despite these minerals, adequate consumption of plant foods cannot fulfill the human body’s total nutrient requirement.

facts.claim: Diets predominantly vegetarian are composed of components that inhibit mineral bioavailability, and this inhibition is predominant.
facts.quote: Diets predominantly vegetarian are composed of components that enhance as well as inhibit mineral bioavailability, the latter being predominant.

facts.claim: Increases in Fe, Zn and Ca absorption have been reported in adults fed dephytinized cereals compared with cereals containing their native phytate.
facts.quote: Increases in Fe, Zn and Ca absorption have been reported in adults fed dephytinized cereals compared with cereals containing their native phytate.

facts.claim: Fruits such as mango and papaya, when consumed in combination with milk, provide significantly higher amounts of bioavailable β-carotene.
facts.quote: Fruits such as mango and papaya, when consumed in combination with milk, provide significantly higher amounts of bioavailable β-carotene.

facts.claim: Plant foods contain anti-nutritional factors like phytate, tannins, phenols, and oxalates that can compromise the bioavailability of several essential micronutrients.
facts.quote: Plant foods also contain ample amounts of anti-nutritional factors such as phytate, tannins, phenols, oxalates, etc. These factors can compromise the bioavailability of several essential micronutrients in plant foods.

research.angle: While plant-based diets are associated with micronutrient deficits due to predominant anti-nutritional factors, specific processing methods and food combinations can improve the bioavailability of these nutrients.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that plant-based diets face significant bioavailability challenges from anti-nutrients, but these can be mitigated through specific processing and culinary combinations.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide specific data on the long-term physiological decline of individuals on modern 'clean' diets.
